accuracy.evidence: Checked CCSS 2.NBT.1 / 2.NBT.1a: three digits as hundreds, tens, ones; 100 as ten tens; zero holding a place in numbers like 305.

misconceptions.evidence: Checked traps: digit-sum (347 as 14); swapped places; hundreds digit read as tens/ones; ignoring zero as place holder (305 as 35).

lab_distinct.evidence: Checked flag3digit: H–T–O expand/build; not flag2digit (two places), flaghund (count hops), flagm100 (multiples of 100), flagtenten (10 tens↔1 hundred).

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked: learner builds 241, expands 347, names hundreds worth, reads 305 with zero, spots digit-sum myth, builds 516.

predictions.evidence: Checked tempting wrongs on 241 value, 347 expansion, hundreds-digit worth, zero-place 305, digit-sum myth, and 516 compose.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked why() splits digit-sum, place-swap, hundreds-as-tens, zero-as-decoration, and true place-value oks.

readability.evidence: Checked ages 7–8 kid lines use hundreds / tens / ones; adult names CCSS 2.NBT.1 and common slips within family bars.

no_filler.evidence: Checked every sentence teaches three-digit place value, expansion, zero holding a place, or a named mix-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked H–T–O Add hundred/ten/one buttons and large choice lbtns; layout holds near 390 px width.

accessibility.evidence: Checked Add-hundred/ten/one buttons twin every H–T–O canvas tap; live aria-label describes the chart; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: CCSS 2.NBT.1 Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones
UK NC 2013 Maths Y3 recognise the place value of each digit in a three-digit number (hundreds, tens, ones)
